packageRules.description: Runtime dependencies are ranges, not pins, because users resolve them fresh on every install; our lockfile isn't published. Pinning them would hold users on whatever versions our last release happened to have, including a Lighthouse that no longer works with current Chrome. update-lockfile still opens a PR for each in-range release, so CI tests the same versions users are getting, and those lockfile-only PRs are safe to automerge because they change nothing in the published package. A new major falls outside the range, gets a PR that rewrites it, and isn't automerged; that one ships to users, so it needs a changeset.
csv-parse and csv-stringify move their export paths together, and both are imported from the same modules here.

@types/node should track the oldest supported Node version from engines, not the newest, so that APIs unavailable on the floor fail to type-check. Raise this when the engines floor rises above Node 22.
typescript-eslint declares typescript '>=4.8.4 <6.1.0', so TypeScript 7 breaks linting. Remove this once typescript-eslint supports the TS 7 compiler.
